brief: Five-part GS Morning roundup. Asia equities sold off overnight (KOSPI -5-6%, Nikkei -1.5-2%, Taiwan -2%, Samsung/Hynix -7-10%) on CXMT memory concerns, but five stocks drove the entire Nikkei decline while TOPIX rose, signaling a crowded-position unwind rather than indiscriminate selling. GS's equity trading desk argues this is not bearish for aggregate AI compute demand. Microsoft's Maia 300 chips moving to TSMC's 2nm process hurts merchant GPU suppliers but helps custom silicon, Broadcom and Intel reaffirmed multi-year demand through 2030, and Meta's Muse Wonder looks competitive, meaning more frontier competition drives more compute need. The real risk GS flags is capacity and power delivery lagging expectations, pressuring AI capex valuations. Separately, GS's rates team says a Fed repricing from cuts to hikes, amid rising inflation risk and reduced labor concern since the US-Iran conflict, explains most of this year's UST yield rise, yet argues yields now look cheap enough to turn bullish on duration. Hungary's government is expected to release a medium-term budget around October 15-20 targeting a deficit below 3% of GDP by 2029, implying a 2031 euro-adoption path without a formal commitment. GS's structured products desk is also pitching dual notes betting on equities up and EURUSD down.
